title: Stephan 2026: superlinear complexity of the (3/2)^n steering word
abstract: A minimal Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of R. Stephan, Superlinear complexity of the (3/2)^n steering word (arXiv:2607.11648), built on the repository's libraries ArithmeticHeights and DiophantineApproximation, whose p-adic Subspace Theorem it uses. Write (3/2)^n = m_n + ε_n with m_n the nearest integer and t_n = 2 m_{n+1} − 3 m_n. The library Stephan2026a is sorry-free and within Lean's three standard axioms. It proves Theorem 1.1, the subword complexity p_T(k) of the steering word T = (t_n) satisfies p_T(k)/k → ∞, together with the numbered results on its proof path: the repetition identity and its corollaries (§2), the reduction to the Diophantine kernel (K) (§3), and the kernel itself, by Ridout-type and three-variable applications of the Subspace Theorem (§4). The open problems of §5 and Conjecture A.2 are stated in Stephan2026a/Problems.lean. Two statements are compared, both forms of Theorem 1.1.
